SESAME_DRIVER: The protocol SESAME uses to verify identities: `cas`, `gateway`, `oauth2`, `oidc` or `fake`
SESAME_CAS_BASE_URL: The CAS server's base URL (no trailing slash, including the path the server lives under; Academica is `/cas`)
SESAME_CAS_SERVICE_URL: The URL the CAS server sends the user back to after verifying them
SESAME_CAS_PROTOCOL: The CAS protocol version; set `3.0` when the server releases attributes on `/p3/serviceValidate`
SESAME_CAS_RENEW: Send `renew=true`; leave off against Academica, which issues no ticket for it
SESAME_CAS_ASSUME_MFA: Count a successful validation as an MFA sign-in; on only when the CAS server enforces MFA for every sign-in
SESAME_CAS_REQUIRE_PENDING_LOGIN: Require that this browser started the sign-in before a CAS ticket is accepted (blocks login CSRF); turn off only for CAS-initiated entry
SESAME_FAKE_USERNAME: The identity the `fake` driver returns, for local development
SESAME_GATEWAY_HEADER: The header the Drawbridge gateway sends its signed JWT assertion in
SESAME_GATEWAY_PUBLIC_KEY: The gateway's public key: a PEM string or a path to one for ES256 and RS256, a base64-encoded raw key or a path to one for EdDSA
SESAME_GATEWAY_ISSUER: The issuer claim the gateway assertion must carry
SESAME_GATEWAY_AUDIENCE: The audience claim the gateway assertion must carry
SESAME_GATEWAY_LEEWAY_SECONDS: Clock skew allowed on the assertion's time claims, in seconds
SESAME_GATEWAY_TRUSTED_PROXIES: Comma-separated CIDR ranges (or single IPs) the gateway proxy sits behind; the request must come from one of them
SESAME_GATEWAY_MAX_LIFETIME: The longest an assertion may live, in seconds; longer ones are refused
SESAME_GATEWAY_REPLAY_STORE: The cache store used jtis are kept in, so a captured assertion cannot be replayed
SESAME_GATEWAY_ALLOW_WITHOUT_REPLAY_GUAR: Skip the replay guard entirely; local development only, never in production
SESAME_OAUTH2_ISSUER: The issuer of the JWT bearer tokens (Microsoft Entra ID first: the tenant's v2.0 endpoints)
SESAME_OAUTH2_JWKS_URL: The issuer's key set (JWKS) the tokens are verified against
SESAME_OAUTH2_AUDIENCE: The audience claim the token must carry (for Entra, the app's client id)
SESAME_OAUTH2_LEEWAY_SECONDS: Clock skew allowed on the `exp` and `nbf` checks, in seconds
SESAME_OAUTH2_IDENTITY_CLAIM: The claim the username comes from: `preferred_username` or `accessid`
SESAME_OAUTH2_JWKS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS: How long the fetched key set is kept, in seconds; refetched at most once a minute for an unknown key id
SESAME_OAUTH2_JWKS_STORE: The cache store the key set is kept in
SESAME_OAUTH2_REQUIRE_AT_JWT: Check the access token's `typ` header is `at+jwt` or `application/at+jwt`; off because Microsoft Entra v2 tokens are typed `JWT`
SESAME_OIDC_ISSUER: The OpenID Connect issuer for browser sign-in (Microsoft Entra ID first)
none (falls back to `SESAME_OAUTH2_ISSUER`; Playbook supplies the WSU value)
SESAME_OIDC_CLIENT_ID: The provider app registration's client id
SESAME_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET: The provider app registration's client secret; read from the environment only, never logged
SESAME_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI: The redirect URI; must be registered on the app registration as a Web redirect URI
SESAME_OIDC_SCOPES: The scopes requested on the authorization call, space-separated
SESAME_OIDC_CLIENT_AUTH: Client authentication on the token call: `client_secret_post` or `client_secret_basic`
SESAME_OIDC_USERNAME_CLAIM: The ID token claim the username comes from
SESAME_OIDC_USERNAME_FALLBACK: Use the `preferred_username` prefix when the username claim is missing; off because preferred_username is user-changeable
SESAME_OIDC_ROLES_CLAIM: The ID token claim the roles come from (a JSON list)
SESAME_OIDC_CLAIMS: The ID token claims passed through to the user resolver as identity attributes, comma-separated
SESAME_OIDC_ASSUME_MFA: Count an OIDC sign-in as an MFA sign-in
SESAME_OIDC_LEEWAY_SECONDS: Clock skew allowed on the ID token's time claims, in seconds
SESAME_OIDC_POST_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URI: When set, logout sends the user through the provider's end-session endpoint
SESAME_OIDC_AUTHORIZATION_ENDPOINT: Override the authorization endpoint from the discovery document
SESAME_OIDC_TOKEN_ENDPOINT: Override the token endpoint from the discovery document
SESAME_OIDC_JWKS_URI: Override the JWKS URI from the discovery document
SESAME_OIDC_END_SESSION_ENDPOINT: Override the end-session endpoint from the discovery document
SESAME_OIDC_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS: How long the discovery document and key set are cached, in seconds
SESAME_OIDC_CACHE_STORE: The cache store the discovery document and key set are kept in
SESAME_OIDC_STEP_UP_PROMPT: The `prompt` parameter a step-up login request adds
SESAME_OIDC_STEP_UP_MAX_AGE: The `max_age` parameter a step-up login request adds
SESAME_OIDC_STEP_UP_ACR_VALUES: The `acr_values` parameter a step-up login request adds
SESAME_OIDC_STEP_UP_CLAIMS: The `claims` parameter a step-up login request adds
SESAME_SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES: The idle timeout in minutes: the quiet time after which the session is dropped
SESAME_SESSION_ABSOLUTE_MINUTES: The absolute lifetime in minutes: the longest a session may live, no matter how active it is
SESAME_MFA_MAX_AGE: How long a verified MFA sign-in stays good, in seconds
SESAME_MFA_ON_FAILURE: What the `sesame.mfa` middleware does when the check fails: `deny` answers 403, `reauth` sends the user back to the login route
SESAME_ROUTES: Register GET `/login`, POST `/logout` and (for oidc) GET `/login/callback`; false keeps the routes in the app's own route file
SESAME_LOG: Log sign-in and sign-out events through the app's PSR-3 logger
SESAME_USER_RESOLVER: The class that turns a verified identity into the app's user; it must implement `Waynestate\Sesame\UserResolver`
